name: spondyloarthritis overview
title: Spondyloarthritis: inflammatory back pain points to ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis to psoriatic arthritis, and a gut or genital infection weeks before to reactive arthritis; each column gives presentation, exam and tests, and treatment in order, with the SpA features, classification criteria and psoriatic vs rheumatoid arthritis below

root.title: Inflammatory back pain or lower-limb oligoarthritis, rheumatoid factor NEGATIVE: which spondyloarthritis (SpA)?
lines: SpA features: inflammatory back pain · arthritis · enthesitis (heel) · anterior uveitis · dactylitis · psoriasis · Crohn's or colitis · good response to NSAIDs · family history · HLA-B27 · raised CRP
imaging: sacroiliitis on X-ray or MRI · predisposing: infection (Chlamydia) · psoriasis · Crohn's, ulcerative colitis
family: ankylosing spondylitis · psoriatic · reactive · arthritis with Crohn's or ulcerative colitis · acute anterior uveitis · undifferentiated · juvenile (enthesitis-related)

groups.title: Gut or genital infection 1-3 weeks before

head: h
Ankylosing spondylitis
the prototype · HLA-B27 in > 90% (white patients)
but 8% of white people carry HLA-B27
HLA-B27+ = 50-100× the risk · prevalence 0.1-1.4%
pres: Starts at the sacroiliac joints, climbs
• can start as a lower-limb oligoarthritis
• iliac crests, trochanters, patellae, pubic symphysis, manubriosternal joint, clavicles
• Aortitis, aortic regurgitation, conduction block, pericarditis
• Pulmonary: upper-lobe fibrosis · Ocular: anterior uveitis 25-30%
inv: bilateral, symmetric: iliac-side erosion → sclerosis → fusion
bone marrow edema (dark T1, bright STIR) = non-radiographic axial SpA
tx: ~ potentially disease modifying · watch the gut
Conventional DMARDs do NOT work in the spine

head: h
Psoriatic arthritis
5-7% of people with psoriasis · axial 2%
HLA-B27, B38, B39, DR4
first-degree relatives 50× the risk
pres: • arthritis first or together in ⅓
• hidden: scalp, navel, behind ears, perianal, nails
• mostly distal finger joints 5-10% · arthritis mutilans 5%
inv: • oil spots, splinter hemorrhages, red lunula
tx: ~ little proof they stop X-ray progression
• IL-12/23: skin +++, joints · NOT the spine

head: h
Reactive arthritis
young men, 20-40 · HLA-B27 linked
NOT 'Reiter's syndrome'
pres: • genitourinary: Chlamydia trachomatis, other sexual infections
Can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree
inv: NOT an infection of the joint

panels.title: Inflammatory vs mechanical
items: inflammatory: under 40 · insidious · > 3 months · stiffness > 60 min · night pain · BETTER with activity · sacroiliac tender · lost mobility in all planes · chest expansion ↓ · neuro deficit unlikely
mechanical: any age · acute · < 4 weeks · stiffness < 30 min · no night pain · WORSE with activity · abnormal flexion · normal chest expansion · neuro deficit possible

panels.title: Classification
items: Modified New York (ankylosing spondylitis): X-ray sacroiliitis grade ≥ 2 both sides or 3-4 one side + ≥ 1 clinical: back pain > 3 months, better with exercise, not rest · limited lumbar motion (sagittal + frontal) · limited chest expansion
ASAS axial SpA: back pain ≥ 3 months, onset < 45 → sacroiliitis on imaging (MRI inflammation or definite X-ray) + ≥ 1 SpA feature, OR HLA-B27 + ≥ 2 other SpA features

panels.title: Psoriatic vs rheumatoid
items: ASYMMETRIC 'ray' vs symmetric 'row' · distal finger joints 30-50% vs uncommon
spine: sacroiliac or any level 35% vs neck, late
dactylitis, enthesitis, skin + nails vs nodules, dry eyes and mouth, vasculitis
X-ray: distal erosions + periostitis vs periarticular osteopenia + wrist erosions
